meta.title: ALAKÓL — the Alakol planet · a documentary-digital experience
meta.description: Alakol is not just a resort but a unique territory of natural, ecological and recreational value. What is here, why come, how to get there, where to stay, and who it is for.

pillars.title: Six pillars of uniqueness
pillars.intro: Alakol reveals itself honestly through six features. None of them is a five-star resort — yet they are exactly what makes this place irreplaceable.

geology.title: Geology
geology.body: Eroded, layered shores and healing black pebbles of volcanic-mineral origin. Here stone is part of the therapy, not just scenery.

hydrology.title: Hydrology
hydrology.body: A closed, mineralised lake whose water changes hue along the shore. Its mineral composition and brine are known for their wellness effect.

biodiversity.title: Biodiversity
biodiversity.body: The Alakol Reserve is one of the few nesting grounds on Earth for the relict gull (Larus relictus) and a hub of mass bird migration.

status.title: International status
status.body: Wetlands of international importance (Ramsar Convention) and a key ornithological territory.

landscape.title: Landscape
landscape.body: Nearby lies the Dzungarian Gate, corridor of the Yibe and Yevgey winds. Mountains, steppe and water fit into a single frame.

health.title: Wellness
health.body: Mineral water, black pebbles and climatotherapy. People come here for relief — joints, skin, rest for the body — not for five-star service.

audience.title: Who this place is for — and who it isn't
audience.intro: We don't sell an illusion. It is remote: the sun overhead, wind and dust, heat, infrastructure that is patchy in places. The choice is yours — we give you honest information.

routes.title: Getting there
routes.intro: Departure points, transport, distance and travel time. Figures are approximate — verify before your trip.
routes.note: The main access to the shore is via Usharal; the nearest rail line is Astana–Dostyk.

stays.title: Where to stay
stays.intro: Honest price ranges — this is not Turkey. From guesthouses to first-line camps.
